acceptance.status_reason: ⛔ I NEARLY USED A FALSE ZERO HERE AND CAUGHT IT, WHICH IS WHY THE CENSUS IS SCOPED RATHER THAN WHOLE-BUNDLE. My first probe searched the ENTIRE bundle for the literal 'login#acct#' and got 0 -- which looked like proof the throttle was untouched. It is an ARTIFACT: that string is built at runtime from a template (`${cfg.keyPrefix}#acct#...`) and does not survive minification as a literal. Control proved the throttle IS in the bundle ('#acct#' 1, 'blocked_until' 4, 'auth_throttled' 1). The sound form is the SCOPED one above: absence inside the resend region, with that region's own tokens present as an in-scope positive control. Same class as the wrong-resource-ARN error I made earlier tonight -- a zero produced by the wrong scope, wearing the authority of a measurement.

surprises: ⛔ FINDING AGAINST MY OWN SOURCE, AND IT IS THE SECOND FALSE CLAIM I LEFT IN THIS CODEBASE TONIGHT. The hashCode docstring in mfa.ts read 'so a reader of the table (or of a DynamoDB backup) cannot replay a live challenge.' THAT IS FALSE and the W3-3 exercise refuted it: every code in that run was recovered from the stored row in about a second. Corrected at 1e5e7d4983, with the false sentence QUOTED inside the retraction rather than substituted away -- verified after editing that the phrase survives exactly once, inside the correction. The harm of the old wording was specific: it would have let a future reader wave through a backup-access decision on a guarantee that never held. (The first false claim was email.ts asserting an IAM deny that did not exist.)

OBSERVATION: the ruled fallback for reading a code ('read it from the authoritative MFA table') did not exist, because the table stores only a salted hash. 0.4.0_DE_ClientPlatform~Z measured that before anyone provisioned. The property that makes the system sound is the property that made the fallback impossible -- and the resolution was not a readable mailbox but offline recovery, which retired a HOLD that had been issued on the readable-mailbox premise.

OBSERVATION / DEVIATION DECLARED: the ruling authorised a .invalid fixture; I used success@simulator.amazonses.com instead. .invalid does not resolve, so every send bounces, and bounce rate is scored against opalinvest.dev -- our SOLE verified sending identity, currently HEALTHY, and the domain that expires 2026-12-22. W3-3 requires repeated sends by construction. The simulator is not a human address and equally unreadable, so it satisfies the ruling's intent while removing a cost the ruling did not have in front of it. Flagged in the same turn as the write; the issuing seat can overrule and I re-mint in one call.
